text:
anna: quick q — as we're onboarding another bank for BYOK, do we have a defined cryptographic provenance artifact we store with imports? i.e., a verifiable chain (operator sigs, firmware hash, attestation token) that we persist in audit logs?
ritesh: short answer: not a single standard today. we capture some bits (operator id, import method, HSM model, import-time nonce) but not a compact provenance bundle.
mia: +1, customers keep asking for an evidence chain for audits. legal also asked about chain-of-custody records yesterday.
sam: what would that bundle look like in practice? JSON schema we can shove into the audit event? or an external signed blob?
anna: thinking both — embed a minimal index in our audit log (key_id, provenance_ref, attestation_summary) and store the full signed blob in an append-only store (s3 with immutability / ledger).
ritesh: prototype schema i sketched this morning — can someone sanity-check?
ritesh: ```json
{"key_id":"tenant/123/key-abc","imported_by":"ops-jen","operators":["ops-jen","sam"],"hsm_firmware_sha256":"8f3a...","attestation_jwt":"eyJhbGciOi...","timestamp":"2026-03-20T17:12:00Z","handoff_proof":"sig1:sig2"}
```
sam: looks reasonable. two quick notes: 1) don't store full attestation_jwt in plaintext in long-term analytics DB; reference it. 2) include a field for import_method (kek-wrap / transport-key / split-escrow).
ops-jen: fyi i did a manual import for the pilot last month — i can re-run with firmware attestation and add TEE evidence. i want clarity on RBAC before i do more — who needs write access to the provenance store?
mia: RBAC proposal: import-write → limited to operators group; provenance-append → operators + legal-read; provenance-admin → security infra only. also require dual-operator for production imports.
legal: legal here — for regulated customers we need proof of export controls and timestamped custody logs retained 7 years. plus an immutable proof of who had physical access during import window. can we capture that?
ritesh: we can capture operator identity + on-call rotations + ephemeral workstation id in the bundle. physical access may need on-prem witness stamps (photo hash or notary attestation) — that's a separate process.
anna: vuln angle: if the provenance blob is stored in S3 + referenced in DB, we must ensure integrity (SSE-KMS + object lock enabled) and signed metadata. if an attacker could flip the reference to point to another blob, that's bad — DB should store provenance_hash too.
sam: agreed. suggestion: 1) store provenance_blob in immutable bucket, 2) compute sha256(provenance_blob) and store that hash in the primary audit event (DB row), 3) sign the hash with our infra key before writing.
ritesh: ops requirements: who can read the blob? readonly for customer support, legal, and tenant auditors. redaction: redact operator personal emails from public exports.
ops-jen: oncall implications — if import fails or attestation mismatch, what is the incident workflow? do we roll back import, quarantine key, or proceed with rollback to previously-in-use key?
anna: tentative workflow: 1) immediate quarantine + hide from routing, 2) create incident with severity P1 if attestation shows firmware mismatch or missing signatures, 3) notify customer and legal, 4) require dual-ops re-import or formal forensics to unblock.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4397 by anna — severity=high — channel=#release-war-room — assigned=ritesh
sam: vuln triage note — if an attacker compromises our DB and swaps provenance_hash but not blob, we still detect mismatch when verifying stored signed hash. need a nightly verification job that re-hashes blobs and ensures signatures match.
ritesh: +1 nightly attestation sweep. add a k8s cronjob that verifies a random sample every hour and full scan nightly. log results to a tamper-evident ledger.
mia: action items: 1) rit: produce a draft provenance JSON schema + retention policy (due EOW) 2) ops-jen: test import with attestation blob and document oncall rollback steps (due mid-next-week) 3) legal: send exact retention + export control language we need to preserve.
legal: will do, will attach a checklist for evidence tags required by auditors.
anna: i'll open a confluence page and a quick RFC for RBAC changes (dual-op, groups, read-grants) — link back here once ready.
sam: one more question — KMS integration: for objects we store encrypted with SSE-KMS, do we use tenant CMK or our infra CMK? customer usually prefers tenant CMK when available. thoughts?
ritesh: prefer tenant CMK for customer-visible blob contents; infra CMK for index/metadata in multi-tenant DB. need to document key-policy exceptions for cross-account verification/forensics.
ops-jen: ok i'll stage a test import using tenant CMK encryption and report any permission gaps.
anna: thanks all — keeping this thread as the canonical spot for provenance design. if anyone has references (NIST 800-57, ISO 19790) post them here. :thumbsup:
sam: posting the NIST fragment we referenced earlier — https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-57pt1r5.pdf
ritesh: i'll follow up with a lightweight PoC repo for schema + sample verification script.
anna: perfect. closing loop for today.
